archetype.name: Point Guard (late-career)
archetype.definition: At 42, Rodgers runs a quick, horizontal distribution offense that wins between the numbers and inside 10 yards but can no longer threaten defenses vertically.

report.headline: Touchdowns and volume hide an offense that stalls everywhere beyond ten yards.
report.take:
The box score says a productive veteran: 247.8 yards a game (11th), 12 touchdowns (4th) and a 4-2 record. The efficiency says otherwise. His -0.109 EPA per dropback ranks 33rd of 45, and his -4.6 passing EPA a game ranks 35th. Two things explain the gap. Mike McCarthy's offense passes far more than game state calls for, ranking 3rd in pass rate over expected, so the counting stats come from volume, not quality. And the Steelers keep getting into the red zone, where he has 8 touchdowns even though his red-zone EPA is -0.174.

The passing game splits cleanly in two. Short and middle, he still plays at a high level: +0.18 EPA on throws of 0-9 air yards with a +6.3 CPOE, and +0.571 EPA on throws to the middle. Downfield it falls apart. He has completed 18.8% of his 20+ yard throws with a -16.1 CPOE, and screens and throws behind the line have cost -12 EPA. The defining problem is the sack-and-stall cycle. He is pressured on only 17.4% of dropbacks (9th-lowest), yet 32.6% of those pressures become sacks (27th of 37). Eleven of his 19 sacks came on third down, where his EPA is -0.38 and the conversion rate is 30.3%. He also holds the ball longer than last year, 2.75 seconds against 2.59.

None of this is a sudden collapse. The career line shows a steady slide since 2021: EPA per play of 0.041, 0.058 and 0.064 over 2022, 2024 and 2025, a pressure-to-sack rate that was already 38th of 62 last season, and an aDOT that kept shrinking. What is new is that the floor has dropped below average. His CPOE (-0.96) and completion rate (61.4%, down 4.3 points) both took a step back. The last three games were better (-0.052 EPA per dropback, +0.5 CPOE), but Tampa Bay's 4th-ranked defense held him to 3.6 intended air yards and -13.5 EPA.

The supporting cast is now the bigger story. Michael Pittman (78% of snaps) and Roman Wilson are both on IR. Wilson had been his most efficient target at 0.254 EPA per target. That leaves DK Metcalf, who has drawn 51 targets at only 0.04 EPA each, plus rookie Germie Bernard, Jaylen Warren and Pat Freiermuth. Without Wilson, expect an even shorter, more Freiermuth-and-backfield passing game.

strengths.title: Short-area accuracy and timing
strengths.body: Within 10 air yards he is still precise and on schedule: a +6.3 CPOE and +0.18 EPA on short throws, with 8 of his 12 touchdowns. It reflects pre-snap processing, which ages better than arm strength. It should hold all season.

strengths.title: Owns the middle of the field
strengths.body: Throws between the numbers produce +0.571 EPA and a 58% success rate, by far his best cut. Those are anticipation throws over linebackers, and they are where Freiermuth (0.176 EPA per target) lives. The sample is 50 attempts, but it matches his short-game profile.

strengths.title: Volume-driven fantasy floor
strengths.body: A pass-heavy scheme keeps him at 38.8 attempts a game and a 34-touchdown pace. His yardage is up 40.2 a game from last season. As long as McCarthy keeps throwing, the counting stats outrun the efficiency.

concerns.title: Sacks kill drives on third down
concerns.body: Pressure is rare, but when it arrives a third of it becomes a sack. Eleven sacks on third down have produced -25.1 EPA in that situation alone. This is long-running: the pressure-to-sack rate was 34.1% last season, so it reflects how he now plays, not bad luck.

concerns.title: No vertical game
concerns.body: His 32 deep attempts have produced a 18.8% completion rate and a -16.1 CPOE. Throws of 10+ yards overall are completed 35.2% of the time. With the deep threat gone, defenses can squat on the short game, which is exactly what Tampa Bay did.

concerns.title: Receiving corps thinned by IR
concerns.body: Wilson's 0.254 EPA per target was the best on the team, and Pittman was a 78%-snap starter. Both are out until mid-to-late November. Metcalf has been near break-even per target. The remaining group lacks someone who wins outside, so the offense will likely get even more horizontal.

trend.note: His game EPA has swung from -21.4 at New England to three straight positive games against mid-pack defenses, then back to -13.5 against Tampa Bay's 4th-ranked unit. The last three games are better than his season (+0.057 EPA per dropback), but the results still track the opponent more than any real improvement.

nextGame.headline: A leaky, banged-up Saints defense suits his short game.
nextGame.body:
New Orleans is the right kind of opponent. The Saints rank 27th in defensive EPA and dead last in success rate allowed, and they give up 275.7 passing yards a game (27th). They also generate little pressure (25th in hit rate), which matters for a quarterback whose problem is converting pressure into sacks, not avoiding it. Opposing WR1s have scored 3.1 PPR over their averages (26th), a direct opening for Metcalf. Tight ends draw 30% of targets against this defense versus 23.7% league-wide, which points to Freiermuth over the middle. The Saints are also 31st against deep passes, but that is the one area Rodgers has not shown he can exploit. The Book has Pittsburgh -3.5 with a 44.5 total, and the game is indoors (reported to be in Paris).

The Saints' injuries help him. LB Kaden Elliss (100% of snaps) and DT Nathan Shepherd are out, which weakens the second-level coverage and interior push that defend his favorite middle throws. Both starting corners, Kool-Aid McKinstry and Quincy Riley (about 90% of snaps each), are questionable. On his side, Wilson and Pittman are on IR and Ben Skowronek is out, so his targets narrow to Metcalf, Bernard, Freiermuth and Warren.

keyMatchups.title: Freiermuth against a LB corps missing Elliss
keyMatchups.body: The Saints funnel targets to tight ends and will be without their every-down linebacker. That lines up with Rodgers' best area, the middle of the field. Expect Freiermuth to be the volume leader.

keyMatchups.title: Metcalf against questionable corners
keyMatchups.body: Opposing WR1s have outscored their averages against New Orleans, and both starting corners carry injury tags. Metcalf has had volume without efficiency. A depleted secondary is his best chance to change that.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots against the 31st deep defense
keyMatchups.body: The Saints allow 1.4 EPA on deep throws, one of the worst marks in the league. Rodgers, though, has completed fewer than one in five deep attempts. Whether this matchup produces chunk plays or just more misses is the swing in his ceiling.

nextGame.watch: Whether he takes deep shots against the league's 31st deep defense, or settles for 4-yard throws the way he did in Tampa.

restOfSeason.body:
Volume is the stable part. McCarthy's pass-first lean and Rodgers' short-game accuracy should keep him around 240-270 yards a game with a low-end QB1 or high-end QB2 fantasy floor. The touchdown rate is the most likely thing to come down. A 5.2% TD rate built on red-zone plays that are losing EPA overall rarely holds, so expect closer to 1.5-2 a game than 2. The sacks and the dead deep game are long-standing traits that age only makes worse, so efficiency will stay below average.

The outlook improves in late November if Pittman and Wilson come back on schedule. Until then, the passing game rests on Metcalf finding efficiency and Freiermuth carrying the middle. Matchups will drive the week-to-week swings: soft defenses like New Orleans produce his 22-point games, while top units shut down the short game and pile up sacks.
swingFactors: Timing of Pittman and Wilson's returns from IR
Whether any deep passing game appears
Third-down sack rate against good pass rushes

confidence.note: Six games, but his traits match a multi-year career decline. The receiver injuries add role uncertainty.
